They're not mutually exclusive, sometimes Shenmue fans aren't bothered by (or actually like) QTEs. But I'm talking about the praise (that's linked to nostalgia) it receives, and received at the reveal of Shenmue 3 kickstarter. Hell, [they received $6.3 million out of the $2 mill. they were asking for](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ysnet/shenmue-3/description), but I bet my dog's skin that not every backer actually likes QTEs.

So, what's up with that?
[DISCUSSION] Why do a lot of people praise Shenmue if it has QTEs, another hated thing in the gaming industry?

Have you heard of helldivers? It's basically an average twin-stick shooter + QTEs. Everything that makes it interesting is tied to entering in a timed button combo of somewhere around 5-10 keys, which it has you do incessantly. It's currently "very positive" on steam. I hate QTEs too, but there are apparently a lot of people who like them.

I have, but I didn't know it had QTEs. I didn't even see them. Do you mean the ones at the start of the game? (for reference, the guy's dropping emergency beacons on the bottom left).

And well, if those are QTEs, anything can be considered QTEs. A CS:GO player pointing his AWP at the head of another head and then shooting is a QTE, because it's an event and he has to be quick with his time, or else he dies.
It's entering a lengthy, arbitrary button combo that has zero decision making involved other than "Press the button you're told to press". That is not even kind of like playing an FPS.
Are those the QTEs from the Helldivers video though? I just don't see them. You have to do it once at the start of the game. Then it's free-roaming.

You do it every time you call in any equipment or interact with anything. The guy in that video does it a lot more than once, and objective based missions rather than boss missions like that have you do it a lot more often.

Yeah sure it's a QTE in and of itself, but it's a component in the game, and not the "main" game as in games like Shenmue (the main game being shooting the shit out of aliens).

If you had to ask a Helldivers fan what do they do in the game, I'm pretty sure the first thing they'd blur out is not "QTEs".

My point isn't that it's all QTEs, my point is that "It's basically an average twin-stick shooter + QTEs". If disliking QTEs was really a sufficiently widely held opinion, Helldivers would not have been positively received, because the primary thing differentiating it from it's competition is QTEs. I don't like QTEs, so I consider it entirely inferior to, say, Alien Swarm, a free game from six years ago.

Idk man, personally QTEs don't seem to be part of the main game to me, so the fact that Helldivers is so famous is because of the shooting, not the QTEs.

And Alien Swarm was awesome, so sad Valve stopped giving a shit about it. :/

It's not that people liked the QTEs, it's everything else about the game that worked.

Mostly it's the world it presents, it's a period piece that accurately recreates Japan in the era it's set in [at least a reasonable approximation anyway]. At the time, most people who were into games enough to play something like Shenmu were also the same people who were really into Anime.

Wandering around the town, doing all sorts of Otaku activities as well as taking in the culture was a part of the experience outside of the game's storyline. Honestly, the story wasn't great and was really kind of generic. The world was the big draw, and people put up with the QTE mechanic because the rest of it was so interesting.

In my experience, most people who play the game spend most of their time goofing off in the town and only progress the story to unlock things.
Probably not a problem because QTEs started with Shenmue. Fits well with the pacing of the story.
